subject: sociology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: What is a nuclear family?
options: Two generations – a couple and their dependent children – living together
Three or more generations living in the same household
A lone parent living with their children
A married couple living without any children
questions.explain: A nuclear family is the two-generation unit of a couple and their dependent children.

questions.q: The Khan household contains grandparents, their married son and his wife, and their two children, all under one roof. Which family form is this?
questions.explain: An extended family adds relatives beyond the nuclear unit, such as grandparents, within one household.

questions.q: According to Murdock (1949), which four functions does the family perform for society?
questions.explain: Murdock argued the family universally meets sexual, reproductive, economic and educational needs.

questions.q: What is a beanpole family?
options: A multi-generational family that is long and thin, with few children in each generation
A family with many children in a single generation
A family with no living grandparents
questions.explain: A beanpole family extends vertically across several generations but has few members in each.

questions.q: After her divorce, Maria marries Tom, who brings his young son to live with Maria and her daughter. What type of family have they formed?
questions.explain: A reconstituted (step) family forms when a new couple unites and at least one partner brings a child.

questions.q: Which of these best describes the process of primary socialisation carried out by the family?
options: Teaching children the basic norms and values of their society
Providing children with a formal school qualification
Enforcing the laws of the state
questions.explain: Primary socialisation is the family's role in teaching children society's core norms and values.

questions.q: Which sociologist claimed that the nuclear family is universal, found in some form in every society?
questions.explain: Murdock claimed, from his study of 250 societies, that the nuclear family is universal.

questions.q: Parsons argued the modern family performs two 'basic and irreducible' functions. What are they?
options: Primary socialisation of children and stabilisation of adult personalities
questions.explain: Parsons said the family primarily socialises children and stabilises adult personalities.

questions.q: Parsons' 'warm bath theory' is used to explain which family function?
options: Stabilising adult personalities by relieving the stresses of daily life
Providing children with an economic income
questions.explain: The 'warm bath' image describes how the family soothes adults and stabilises their personalities.

questions.q: In Parsons' view, what is the difference between the instrumental and expressive roles in the family?
options: The instrumental role is the breadwinner; the expressive role is the caring, emotional role
The instrumental role is emotional; the expressive role earns money
Both roles involve only paid work
Both roles are shared equally by all family members
questions.explain: Parsons linked the male instrumental (breadwinner) role and the female expressive (caring) role.

questions.q: Which statement best sums up the Marxist view of the family?
options: The family benefits capitalism by socialising children to accept inequality and reproducing labour
The family exists to meet the emotional needs of all its members equally
The family is naturally symmetrical and egalitarian
The family has no economic role in society
questions.explain: Marxists argue the family serves capitalism by reproducing and conditioning an obedient workforce.

questions.q: Feminists most commonly criticise the family for being:
options: Patriarchal, benefiting men at the expense of women
questions.explain: Feminists argue the family is patriarchal, serving men's interests over women's.

questions.q: Which sociologists described the modern 'symmetrical family', in which partners' roles are more equal?
questions.explain: Willmott and Young identified the symmetrical family, with more shared and balanced roles.

questions.q: What are 'segregated' conjugal roles?
options: Roles where partners have clearly separate tasks and leisure activities
Roles where partners share all tasks equally
Roles based on religious duty alone
questions.explain: Segregated conjugal roles involve partners keeping their tasks and leisure clearly separate.

questions.q: Which of the following best helps explain the rise in divorce rates in many societies?
options: Changes in the law, secularisation and greater independence for women
A fall in the number of marriages taking place
A decline in women working outside the home
questions.explain: Easier divorce laws, weaker religious influence and women's independence have all raised divorce rates.

questions.q: The idealised image of the typical family shown in adverts – a married couple with two children – is often called the:
questions.explain: The 'cereal packet family' describes the idealised nuclear image used in advertising.

questions.q: In the Ahmed household, both partners work, share the cooking and childcare, and make decisions together. Which term best describes their conjugal roles?
questions.explain: Joint conjugal roles involve partners sharing tasks and decisions, as in a symmetrical family.

questions.q: Rapoport and Rapoport are best known for arguing that modern families are characterised by:
options: Increasing diversity, with many different family types
A single dominant nuclear family type
A return to the extended family
The disappearance of the family altogether
questions.explain: Rapoport and Rapoport stressed growing family diversity rather than one 'normal' family type.

questions.q: The feminist idea of the 'dual burden' refers to women who:
options: Do paid work and also carry out most of the housework and childcare
Refuse to do any domestic work
Only do paid work outside the home
Share all housework equally with their partner
questions.explain: The dual burden is the double load of paid employment plus unpaid domestic work borne by women.

questions.q: A sociologist studying domestic violence and the abuse of children within families is investigating what critics call the:
questions.explain: The 'dark side' of the family highlights abuse and violence that can occur behind closed doors.
